title: Microstructural Characterization of Nb-Added Maraging 18Ni Steel
content: Maraging steels are high-strength alloys widely utilized in applications requiring both strength and toughness. These steels undergo precipitation hardening and must be subjected to solution heat treatment followed by aging to achieve their maximum strength potential. However, thermal aging leads to a significant reduction in toughness [1]. Conventional maraging steels contain 18% Ni, along with additions of Mo and Ti, which promote precipitation hardening. The Ni3Ti and Fe2Mo precipitates are primarily responsible for the increase in mechanical strength during aging [1,2], with the intensity of hardening being adjustable according to the Mo and Ti content in the alloy. Additionally, the presence of 8 to 10% Co enhances the response to age hardening by reducing Mo solubility [4]. However, due to the high cost of Co, some variants of maraging steels without this element have been studied and produced [3,4]. Lee et al. [5] reported a significant improvement in mechanical properties with small Nb additions to maraging steels. More recently, Parvinian et al. [6] observed that Nb and B micro-additions contributed to a reduction in martensite packet size, leading to an improvement in the mechanical properties of 18% Ni maraging steels.
